_comment: The ONE edit point. Add a product here (one object) + drop its page at <id>/index.html and the landing picks it up. No per-page hand-edit.

products.title: Pay in-feed (Farcaster / Base mini app)
products.what: A pay link inside a Farcaster cast or Base mini app: tap, pay USDC on Base, receipt in the thread. The deposit address is derived live from the P2 Registry's predict(), and the fee is read live on-chain.
products.fee: 500 bps on each forwarded payment (the P2 Registry's fee, paid by the forwarder the link derives) — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the mini app, paste or make a pay link, tap Pay.
products.chains_note: `contract` above is the BASE v2 (audit-fix) address — redeployed 2026-11-09, Base ONLY. The v1 Registry 0xe9515881fe6976eD9CB55328B8308F6eF7c311a8 stays live on Base, and the other 9 chains still carry the v1 address (v2 is Base-only); never key on the bare string (GOTCHA #95). verify.mjs live-checks the BASE `contract`.
products.role: P2 Registry (the mini app derives its deposit address)

products.title: Micro-payment forwarder
products.what: Register once, get a personal deposit address. Anything sent there auto-forwards to YOUR destination within ~1 block.
products.fee: 500 bps on each forwarded payment — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the page, register a destination, share the address it gives you.
products.chains_note: `contract` above is the BASE v2 (audit-fix) address — redeployed 2026-11-09, Base ONLY. The v1 Registry 0xe9515881fe6976eD9CB55328B8308F6eF7c311a8 stays live on Base, and the other 9 chains still carry the v1 address (v2 is Base-only); never key on the bare string (GOTCHA #95). verify.mjs live-checks the BASE `contract`.

products.title: Escrow as a service
products.what: Lock a token amount against a hashlock or a nominated arbiter, share the escrow address, counterparty releases it — or the payer refunds after the timeout. Funds sit in the escrow contract, never a server.
products.fee: 500 bps on release only, nothing on refund — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the page, create a deal, share the escrow link.
products.chains_note: `contract` above is the BASE v2 (audit-fix) address — redeployed 2026-11-09, Base ONLY. The v1 factory 0x80793a7d35f735bc76BeAf22B1f413926818f410 stays live on Base and is still the factory on optimism; opBNB/gnosis/scroll carry 0x715114076a45c0102Ae3cb38Bcb89B3211ce591f (7794 B, same runtime). verify.mjs live-checks the BASE `contract`.
products.role: EscrowFactory (the only contract a user calls)

products.title: Gas sponsorship (meta-tx relay)
products.what: A merchant integrates us; their users transact gaslessly via an EIP-7702 relay. The user acts, OUR relay pays the gas — the actor/payer split is the whole product.
products.fee: per-sponsored-tx fee to the merchant (>= 1.5x gas floor)
products.start: Read a real sponsored tx on the page: type-4 shape, delegated EOA, actor != payer.

products.title: Receipt NFT (proof-of-payment)
products.what: When a g2b escrow settles, anyone may mint exactly one on-chain receipt NFT to the payer. Fully on-chain tokenURI (base64 JSON) — no server, no IPFS.
products.fee: mintFeeWei = 50000000000000 wei (0.00005 ETH) live; free at deploy — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the page, paste a settled escrow, mint the receipt.

products.title: Slippage-bounded swap router
products.what: An on-chain router that aggregates existing Uniswap V3 + Aerodrome pools (holds no liquidity of its own). Quotes are chosen off-chain; the contract executes the hops it is handed.
products.fee: 5 bps on input, to the treasury
products.start: Open the page, see the per-chain address set and a real quote.
products.chains_note: NOT chain-invariant: this `contract` is the BASE v2 (audit-fix) router — redeployed 2026-11-09, Base ONLY. The v1 Base router 0xEB28D5cA0783D01dd2E4bF86AD7024ca156aB047 stays live; the other 9 chains still carry the v1 router at 0x9651cD591cFe33E1b684e5d8541940e78724c749 (4270 B, unchanged). ⚠ the bare string 0x9651cD591cFe33E1b684e5d8541940e78724c749 on BASE is f1a's RequestRegistry (2772 B), a DIFFERENT contract — never key on the bare string (GOTCHA #95).

products.title: Dust funnel (dust -> USDC)
products.what: Connect a wallet, see scattered dust balances, one click sweeps them to USDC on Base. Non-custodial, stateless contract.

products.title: Payment streams
products.what: Create a streaming payment: a vault drips a token to a recipient over time; the recipient withdraws whatever has vested, permissionlessly.
products.fee: 500 bps, charged only on withdraw — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the page, create a stream or view a live one.
products.chains_note: `contract` above is the BASE v2.1 (dead-drop-fix) factory — deployed 2026-11-10, Base ONLY. v2.1 adds receive()/fallback()/rescue(onlyOwner) + a self-funded create, so a bare send to it is no longer stranded. The superseded v2 0x14bBd99B840a0Bf087b21A31e27BA83B45f958a0 and v1 0x2bB5b763a8A85e446909674177e65cb6F1052b4F stay live on Base (v1 PAUSED; it still holds the existing streams); optimism/opBNB/gnosis/scroll are unchanged (optimism 0x61AB1942a6779D392922cfcd20BA6D7dc36FDe15; opBNB/gnosis/scroll 0xAdB743dA4A5419C62BCc2cF027da6478Ae70f228). ⚠ on arb/polygon/mantle the string 0x61AB1942 holds a DIFFERENT 5143 B contract (an Aave-style vault) that reverts feeBps() — g2a is NOT there (GOTCHA #95). verify.mjs live-checks the BASE `contract`.

products.title: Subscriptions (recurring toll)
products.what: Recurring payments on the SAME factory — no new contract. A payer pre-approves a small allowance; each period a fresh vault is minted for the next window and pulled. A missed period is a HOLE, not a debt.
products.fee: per-period fee to the merchant (live bps read from the factory)
products.start: Open the page, see the live back-to-back periods already fired.
products.chains_note: Same factory as g2a-streams (reused) — the BASE v2.1 address, Base ONLY (see g2a-streams' chains_note for the per-chain set + the 0x61AB1942 collision).

products.title: Payment links
products.what: Create a payment request; you get a URL carrying a deposit address that auto-forwards to you. No account, no wallet, no code. The link is minted by the RequestRegistry and pays a forwarder derived from it.
products.fee: 500 bps on each forwarded payment (the P2 Registry's fee, paid by the forwarder it derives) — live value in the check below
products.start: Open the page, create a request, share the link.

products.title: TypeScript SDK (@fleet/sdk)
products.what: A tree-shakeable viem client: pure {to,data,value} calldata builders for every rail (quote/pay/createLink/createEscrow/release/setMandate/executeLap/swap/sweep/verify402) plus an EIP-712 signing seam. No state at import; addresses are data you pass in.
products.fee: none of its own — the rail it calls charges the fee
products.start: npm i @fleet/sdk; build calldata, simulate, send.

products.title: MCP server (agent tools)
products.what: One line of config gives an agent live, non-custodial rails on Base: one tool per product returns the calldata for the ONE money call and simulates it (dry-run by default) before anything is signed. No API key, no account.
products.fee: none of its own — the rail it calls charges the fee
products.start: Add the dex-fleet MCP server to any MCP client; call a tool.

products.title: x402 facilitator (on-chain 402 gate)
products.what: The on-chain half of an HTTP-402 flow: a server returns 402, the client pays a rail, a gated writer records the settlement, and the server verifies it with a VIEW call then serves the resource. Nothing holds funds.
products.fee: none — the rail that settled the payment charged its fee
products.start: Read the reference server; wire verify() as the gate.

products.title: Settlement registry (read-side paid())
products.what: A read-side mirror of a rail's settlement: a gated writer records paymentId -> (amount, at); anyone reads paid()/isPaid(). markPaid is idempotent, so an id can never silently change meaning.
products.start: Read paid(paymentId) or isPaid(paymentId) after a settle.

products.title: Fleet executor (EIP-7702 batch delegate)
products.what: One installed EIP-7702 delegate drives every fleet surface from a single off-chain EIP-712 signature over a whole batch of (target,value,data) — so the user's own code runs in the user's frame, and any relayer can carry it.
products.fee: none — per-sponsored-tx billing is the paymaster's, next door
products.start: Sign the batch digest off-chain; a relayer calls execute().

products.title: Fleet paymaster (ERC-4337 sponsorship)
products.what: An ERC-4337 v0.7 verifying paymaster that sponsors UserOps calling a fleet contract and charges the sponsorship back as a small additive surcharge on the rail fee (sponsorBps, default 10) — not in ETH. Allow-list + per-sender rate limit. The allow-list is a DECLARATION gate: word 0 of the op's callData is trusted, so a sponsored op can still call a non-listed contract. Rate limit is OFF by default (maxOpsPerWindow == 0 = unlimited).
products.fee: sponsorBps default 10 bps, additive to the rail fee, paid in the RAIL TOKEN not ETH. Owner-settable up to a compiled-in MAX_SPONSOR_BPS = 1000 (10%); lowering it needs a redeploy (constant, no setter). COMBINED worst case = rail fee (<=500 bps) + sponsorBps (<=1000 bps) = 1500 bps (15%); at defaults = 500+10 = 510 bps (5.1%).
products.start: previewSponsorFee(base) to see the surcharge; deposit() to fund (permissionless). Live but was UNFUNDED and UNCONFIGURED at deploy: call deposit() then setAllowedTarget(rail,true) or nothing is sponsored (AA31 until funded; NotAllowedCall until allow-listed).
products.note: live on Base (funded + allow-listed 2026-11-10; stake not yet posted)

products.title: Toll registry (per-product toll lookup)
products.what: A constructor-set, per-chain lookup: product -> (recipient, feeBps, live) in ONE call, so a new product's toll is registered rather than re-derived. A consumer pins the registry's codehash; live=false reverts rather than falling back to a compiled default.
products.fee: none — it reports other products' tolls
products.start: Read toll(product); a consumer divides by the literal 10_000.
